newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower in technical selloff.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower in technical selloff.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled weaker but off the day's lows after late-session bargain-hunting by the trade lifted the spot March contract back towards the middle of the day's range.

Early fund buying carried March to a recent high of 10.89, but the failure to overcome 10.90 snuffed out the bullish sentiment. The buying dried up, clearing the way for the trade to pressure March to the day's low 10.63, dealers said.
"It was like a vacuum. There were no orders resting there of any size," a trader said, noting sell stops under today's low.
The trade appeared on both sides of the market once March rose to 10.65, and locals forced to cover short positions on the close, dealers said.
At least one trader cited overhead selling and said there is more room on the downside.
"I'm inclined to think there is more consolidation between 10.63 and 10.50," he said.
Resistance was pegged over 11.00, where fresh fund buying is likely to emerge.
March closed at 10.71, down 0.15, traded 10.89 to 10.63. The back months settled 0.13 to 0.07 lower.

In fundamental news, players continued to await details of an Iraqi sugar tender. Traders in Jordan said Iraq was considering more than 120 offers from international sugar houses, but there were no signs of an imminent decision.
The tender relates to a $2 million oil-for-food deal approved by the United Nations.
